paper.title: Bias no more: high-probability data-dependent regret bounds for adversarial bandits and MDPs

unmapped: Learning rate tuned with the best arm's loss L*; paper says a doubling trick removes this (Remark 1)
Regret is the realized regret sum_t l_{t,i_t} - min_i sum_t l_{t,i}
settings.definition_quote: For each round $t = 1, \ldots, T$, the learner selects one of the $d$ available actions $i_t \in [d]$, while simultaneously the adversary decides a loss vector $\ell_t \in [0,1]^d$ ... An adaptive adversary can choose $\ell_t$ based on the learner's previous actions ... $\Reg = \sum_{t=1}^T \ell_{t, i_t} - \min_{i \in [d]} \sum_{t=1}^T \ell_{t,i}$

unmapped: Losses normalized so that max_{w in Omega} |<w, l_t>| <= 1
Learner is given a nu-self-concordant barrier for Omega
Regret is realized regret against best fixed action in Omega
settings.definition_quote: Linear bandits generalize MAB from the simplex decision set $\Delta_d$ to an arbitrary convex body $\Omega \subseteq \fR^d$. For each round $t$, the learner selects an action $\wtilde_t \in \Omega$ while simultaneously the adversary decides a loss vector $\ell_t \in \fR^d$, assumed to be normalized such that $\max_{w\in\Omega} |\inner{w, \ell_t}| \leq 1$. ... $\Reg = \max_{u\in\Omega}\sum_{t=1}^T \inner{\wtilde_t - u, \ell_t}$

unmapped: Losses normalized so that max_{w in Omega} |<w, l_t>| <= 1
Learner is given a nu-self-concordant barrier for Omega
Regret is realized regret against best fixed action in Omega
settings.definition_quote: Again, an adaptive adversary can choose $\ell_t$ based on the learner's previous actions, while an oblivious adversary cannot. At the end of round $t$, the learner suffers and only observes loss $\inner{\wtilde_t, \ell_t}$.

source.label: thm:MAB
source.quote: \pref{alg:mab} with a suitable choice of $\eta$ ensures that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\Reg=\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}\big(\sqrt{d\Lstar\ln(\nicefrac{d}{\delta})}+d\ln(\nicefrac{d}{\delta})\big)$, where $\Lstar = \min_i \sum_{t=1}^T \ell_{t,i}$ is the loss of the best arm.

results.notes: Paper's d is number of arms K. Holds against adaptive adversary (union bound over arms in proof). Eta tuning depends on L*; Remark 1 says doubling trick removes this.

tuning: eta = min{1/(640 a C d^2 ln(nu T) ln(C/delta)), 1/(1610 a C d^2 ln(nu T) sqrt(T ln(C/delta)))}

source.label: thm:LB
source.quote: \pref{alg:linear bandit d+1} with a suitable choice of $\eta$ ensures that with probability at least $1-\delta$: $\Reg = \otil\left(d^2\nu\sqrt{ T\ln\frac{1}{\delta}}+d^2\nu\ln\frac{1}{\delta}\right)$, against an oblivious adversary; ...

results.notes: nu is the self-concordance parameter of the barrier (vartheta). Restated as Theorem B.16.

source.label: thm:MDP
source.quote: \pref{alg:MDP} with a suitable choice of $\eta$ ensures that with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\Reg = \otil\left(|X|\sqrt{\Lyr|A| L^{\star}\ln \frac{1}{\delta}}+|X|^5 |A|^2\ln^2 \frac{1}{\delta}\right)$, where $\Lstar = \min_{\pi}\sum_{t=1}^T \ell_t(\pi) \leq \Lyr T$ is the total loss of the best policy.

_verify.summary: The extraction is accurate. The bound expressions, the high-probability qualifiers, the adversary type in each setting and the provenance all match Theorems 2.3, 3.1 and 4.1. The strengthened Freedman inequality (Theorem 2.2) is a technical concentration result and was rightly left out, and the appendix restatements (Theorems B.16 and C.11) add no new results.
